topic: Greek fire — the medieval superweapon that burned on water

beats.narration: Medieval Byzantium had a weapon that burned even on water.
beats.image_prompt: Byzantine warship on dark sea with jets of flame, dramatic night battle atmosphere, cinematic, no people

beats.narration: Greek fire was projected through siphons onto enemy ships. Water did not extinguish it.
beats.image_prompt: close-up of ancient bronze flame siphon nozzle with fire, dramatic sparks, dark background, no people

beats.narration: Its exact recipe was a state secret. It was lost when the empire declined.
beats.image_prompt: ancient sealed scrolls and laboratory vessels on a stone table, candlelight, mysterious mood, no people

beats.narration: Historians still debate the formula — petroleum, resin, and quicklime are common guesses.
beats.image_prompt: burning oil on dark water surface at night, intense flames reflected, cinematic, no people
